name: South Carolina
sources: 2026 law (H.4216, signed March 30, 2026): starts from federal AGI; 1.99% up to $30,000 and 5.21% above for all filing statuses; federal standard and itemized deductions repealed; SC Income Adjusted Deduction $15,000 single/MFS, $22,500 HoH, $30,000 joint, reduced proportionally over federal AGI $40,000-$95,000 / $60,000-$142,500 / $80,000-$190,000; other SC deductions retained: SC Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office fiscal impact statement (scstatehouse.gov/sess126_2025-2026/fiscalimpactstatements/H4216%202026-03-30%20signed.pdf); bill text (scstatehouse.gov/sess126_2025-2026/prever/4216_20260224.htm); SCDOR Individual Income Tax page (dor.sc.gov/iit)
44% net capital gain deduction (long-term gains only) and age-65 deduction of up to $15,000 per person: SCDOR IIT FAQs (dor.sc.gov/iit/prepare-you-file/iit-faqs); SC Code 12-6-1150, 12-6-1140
Dependent exemption $4,930 (2025): SCDOR Individual Income Tax page (dor.sc.gov/iit)
provisional: Dependent exemption $4,930 is the 2025 amount; the indexed 2026 amount was not found
notes: From 2026 South Carolina no longer allows the federal standard or itemized deductions; it uses its own income-adjusted deduction.
The extra deduction for children under 6 and the two-wage-earner credit are not included.
